definitions.english: Saving means keeping some money for later instead of spending it all now.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho beha chelete ka thoko bakeng sa hamorao, ntle le ho e sebelisa kaofela.

definitions.english: When you save, you put money away so you can use it another day.
definitions.sesotho: Ha u boloka, u beha chelete ka thoko hore u e sebelise ka letsatsi le leng.

definitions.english: Saving is like keeping a seed instead of eating it — you keep it for the future.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tshoana le ho boloka peo ho e-na le ho e ja.

definitions.english: Saving means you do not spend all your money today.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela hore ha u sebelise chelete eohle kajeno.

definitions.english: Saving is when you put money in a safe place and do not touch it.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ha u beha chelete sebakeng se sireletsehileng.

definitions.english: Saving is setting aside a portion of your income for future use.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ho behella karolo ea moputso oa hao ka thoko.

definitions.english: Saving means deliberately keeping some money for later needs.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho boloka chelete bakeng sa litlhoko tsa hamorao.

definitions.english: Saving is the habit of putting money aside regularly.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke tloaelo ea ho behella chelete ka thoko hangata.

definitions.english: When you save, you delay spending today so you have money tomorrow.
definitions.sesotho: Ha u boloka, u liehisa tshebeliso kajeno hore u be le chelete hosane.

definitions.english: Saving is the foundation of financial health.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke motheo oa bophelo bo botle ba lichelete.

definitions.english: Saving is the deliberate allocation of income toward future goals.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ho arola moputso ka boomo ho ea lipakaneng tsa bokamoso.

definitions.english: Saving means prioritizing financial security over immediate spending.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho beha tshireletso ea lichelete pele.

definitions.english: Saving is a financial discipline providing liquidity for emergencies.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke taeo ea lichelete e fanang ka chelete ea tshohanyetso.

definitions.english: Saving involves allocating a percentage of income to build reserves.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho kenyelletsa ho arola peresente ea moputso ho haha pokello.

definitions.english: Saving builds financial assets through regular contributions.
definitions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho haha matlotlo a lichelete ka ho kenya chelete hangata.

examples.english: If you get M10 and keep M3 for later, you saved M3.
examples.sesotho: Haeba u fumana M10 mme u boloka M3, u bolokile M3.

examples.english: Your grandmother gives you M5. You put M2 in your piggy bank.
examples.sesotho: Nkhono o u fa M5. U kenya M2 ka piggy bank.

examples.english: A toy costs M50. Saving M10 per week means you will have it in 5 weeks.
examples.sesotho: Sebapadiswa se bitsa M50. Ho boloka M10 ka beke ho bolela hore u tla ba le sona ka libeke tse 5.

examples.english: Instead of spending all your M20, you keep M5.
examples.sesotho: Ho e-na le ho sebelisa M20 eohle, u boloka M5.

examples.english: You have M100 and keep M30 for later.
examples.sesotho: U na le M100 mme u boloka M30 bakeng sa hamorao.

examples.english: You earn M500 and save M100 monthly. After one year, you have M1,200.
examples.sesotho: U fumana M500 mme u boloka M100 ka khoeli. Kamora selemo, u na le M1,200.

examples.english: Your allowance is M300. Set aside M50 before spending anything.
examples.sesotho: Chelete ea hao ke M300. Behella M50 ka thoko pele u sebelisa letho.

examples.english: You need M2,000 for a laptop. Saving M200 monthly means 10 months.
examples.sesotho: U hloka M2,000 bakeng sa laptop. Ho boloka M200 ka khoeli ho bolela likhoeli tse 10.

examples.english: Keep M50 from M200 instead of spending it all.
examples.sesotho: Boloka M50 ho tsoa ho M200 ho e-na le ho e sebelisa eohle.

examples.english: A M1,000 gift: save 30 percent (M300) and spend the rest.
examples.sesotho: Mpho ea M1,000: boloka 30% (M300) mme u sebelise tse setseng.

examples.english: Bursary M2,500: follow 50/30/20 rule, save M500 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Bursary ea M2,500: latela molao oa 50/30/20, boloka M500 ka khoeli.

examples.english: Freelance income M1,500: allocate M300 to savings first.
examples.sesotho: Moputso oa freelance M1,500: arola M300 polokong pele.

examples.english: Save M200 monthly for emergency fund = M2,400 per year.
examples.sesotho: Boloka M200 ka khoeli bakeng sa tshohanyetso = M2,400 ka selemo.

examples.english: Invest M500 monthly at 7 percent = approximately M87,000 in 10 years.
examples.sesotho: Kenya M500 ka khoeli ka 7% = M87,000 ka lilemo tse 10.

examples.english: Income M3,500: M2,000 fixed, M500 savings, M1,000 variable.
examples.sesotho: Moputso M3,500: M2,000 e sa fetoheng, M500 poloko, M1,000 e fetohang.

misconceptions.english: You need lots of money to save — FALSE! Even M1 counts.
misconceptions.sesotho: U hloka chelete e ngata ho boloka — HA SE NNETE! Le M1 e a baloa.

misconceptions.english: Saving is only for rich people — FALSE! Everyone can save.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho boloka ke ha barui feela — HA SE NNETE! Bohle ba ka boloka.

misconceptions.english: Saving means no fun — FALSE! You can save and spend wisely.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho se thabe — HA SE NNETE! U ka boloka le ho sebelisa ka bohlale.

misconceptions.english: Only people with jobs can save — FALSE! Students can too.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba nang le mesebetsi feela ba ka bolokang — HA SE NNETE! Baithuti le bona ba ka boloka.

misconceptions.english: You need M100+ to start — FALSE! M10 regularly adds up.
misconceptions.sesotho: U hloka M100+ ho qala — HA SE NNETE! M10 hangata ea eketsoa.

misconceptions.english: Saving means never spending on yourself — FALSE! It means balance.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bolela ho se ithekele letho — HA SE NNETE! Ho bolela ho lekalekanya.

misconceptions.english: Saving equals investing — FALSE! Different risk levels.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho boloka ho tshoana le matsete — HA SE NNETE! Li na le likotsi tse fapaneng.

misconceptions.english: Save what is left after spending — FALSE! Pay yourself first.
misconceptions.sesotho: Boloka se setseng kamora ho sebelisa — HA SE NNETE! Itefe pele.

misconceptions.english: Inflation makes saving pointless — FALSE! Interest offsets it.
misconceptions.sesotho: Inflation e etsa hore ho boloka ho se thuse — HA SE NNETE! Phaello ea e lekanya.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to learn how to start saving?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u ka rata ho ithuta ho qala ho boloka?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Do you know what a piggy bank is?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u tseba hore na piggy bank ke eng?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to learn about saving goals?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u batla ho ithuta ka lipakane tsa poloko?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Would you like to know where to keep savings?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na u ka rata ho tseba moo u bolokang poloko?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about budgeting too?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue le ka tekanyetso?

how_to.english: Put money in a piggy bank every time you get some.
how_to.sesotho: Kenya chelete ka piggy bank nako le nako ha u e fumana.

how_to.english: Ask your parents to help you open a savings jar.
how_to.sesotho: Kopa batswadi ho u thusa ho bula setshelo sa poloko.

how_to.english: Start with M1 or M2. Even small amounts count!
how_to.sesotho: Qala ka M1 kapa M2. Le chelete e nyane e a baloa!

how_to.english: Set a savings goal, then save a fixed amount each month.
how_to.sesotho: Beha pakane ea poloko, ebe u boloka chelete e behiloeng khoeli le khoeli.

how_to.english: Open a bank savings account and deposit regularly.
how_to.sesotho: Bula akhaonto ea poloko bankeng mme u kene hangata.

how_to.english: Use the 50/30/20 rule: save 20 percent of income.
how_to.sesotho: Sebedisa molao oa 50/30/20: boloka 20% ea moputso.

how_to.english: Automate your savings through a standing order.
how_to.sesotho: Etsa hore poloko e itsamaele ka standing order.

how_to.english: Build an emergency fund with 3-6 months of expenses.
how_to.sesotho: Haha letlole la tshohanyetso ka likhoeli tse 3-6.

how_to.english: Track expenses and identify areas to reduce spending.
how_to.sesotho: Latela litshenyehelo mme u bone moo u ka fokotsang.

why.english: Saving helps you buy things you really want later.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho u thusa ho reka lintho tseo u di batlang hamorao.

why.english: Saving keeps your money safe for the future.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho boloka chelete e sireletsehile bakeng sa bokamoso.

why.english: When you save, you always have money for emergencies.
why.sesotho: Ha u boloka, u lula u na le chelete ea tshohanyetso.

why.english: Saving builds financial security and peace of mind.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho haha tshireletso ea lichelete le kgotso.

why.english: Saving helps you achieve goals like buying a laptop.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho thusa ho fihlela lipakane tse kang ho reka laptop.

why.english: Saving prevents debt when unexpected expenses arise.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho thibela sekoloto ha litshenyehelo tse sa lebellwang li hlaha.

why.english: Saving provides capital for investments and wealth building.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho fana ka motheo oa matsete le ho haha maruo.

why.english: An emergency fund prevents financial crises.
why.sesotho: Letlole la tshohanyetso le thibela mathata a lichelete.

why.english: Saving creates financial independence and options.
why.sesotho: Ho boloka ho bopa boikemelo ba lichelete le likgetho.

situation.english: Mpho gets M20 pocket money. She wants to buy sweets (M5) and a toy (M15). Should she spend all or save some?
situation.sesotho: Mpho o fumana M20 ea pokotho. O batla ho reka lipompong (M5) le sebapadiswa (M15). Na o lokela ho sebelisa tsohle kapa ho boloka tse ding?

advice.english: Mpho should save at least M5. She can buy sweets and save the rest for the toy later.
advice.sesotho: Mpho o lokela ho boloka M5. A ka reka lipompong mme a boloke tse setseng bakeng sa sebapadiswa.

lesson.english: Always save something from what you receive.
lesson.sesotho: Dula u boloka ho hong ho tsoa ho seo u se fumanang.

situation.english: Thabo wants a bicycle that costs M500. He gets M50 pocket money every week. How can he save for it?
situation.sesotho: Thabo o batla baesekele e bitsang M500. O fumana M50 ka beke. A ka e bolokela joang?

advice.english: If Thabo saves M25 per week, he will have M500 in 20 weeks (5 months).
advice.sesotho: Haeba Thabo a boloka M25 ka beke, o tla ba le M500 ka libeke tse 20 (likhoeli tse 5).

lesson.english: Break big goals into smaller weekly savings.
lesson.sesotho: Arola lipakane tse kgolo ka dipoloko tse nyane tsa beke.

situation.english: Lerato earns M600 monthly from part-time work. She spends everything on entertainment. What should she change?
situation.sesotho: Lerato o fumana M600 ka khoeli mosebetsing oa nakwana. O sebelisa tsohle boithabisong. O lokela ho fetola eng?

advice.english: Lerato should save at least M120 (20%). She can still enjoy M480 for other things.
advice.sesotho: Lerato o lokela ho boloka M120 (20%). A ka ntsha M480 bakeng sa lintho tse ding.

lesson.english: Pay yourself first before spending on wants.
lesson.sesotho: Itefe pele pele u sebelisa litakatso.

situation.english: A student gets a M1,000 gift. They want to buy a new phone (M800) and go out with friends (M200). Is this wise?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o fumana mpho ea M1,000. O batla ho reka fono (M800) le ho ea le metswalle (M200). Na see se bohlale?

advice.english: Better plan: Save M300, spend M500 on phone, M200 for friends. Or save M500 and buy a cheaper phone.
advice.sesotho: Leano le betere: Boloka M300, sebelisa M500 fonong, M200 metswalle. Kapa boloka M500 mme u reke fono e theko e tlase.

lesson.english: Balance saving and spending, even with gift money.
lesson.sesotho: Lekalekanya ho boloka le ho sebelisa, le ka chelete ea limpho.

situation.english: A student receives M2,500 bursary monthly. Rent is M1,000, food M800, transport M300. How much should they save?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti o fumana bursary ea M2,500. Rente M1,000, lijo M800, lipalangwang M300. O lokela ho boloka bokae?

advice.english: After expenses: M400 remains. Save M300 and keep M100 for emergencies.
advice.sesotho: Kamora litshenyehelo: M400 e setseng. Boloka M300 mme u boloke M100 bakeng sa tshohanyetso.

lesson.english: Always allocate surplus to savings before discretionary spending.
lesson.sesotho: Dula u arola se setseng polokong pele u sebelisa.

situation.english: A student has no savings and their laptop breaks. They need M3,000 urgently. What went wrong?
situation.sesotho: Moithuti ha a na poloko mme laptop ea hae e senyeha. O hloka M3,000 ka potlako. Ho senyehile eng?

advice.english: Without an emergency fund, unexpected expenses cause debt. Aim to save 3-6 months of expenses.
advice.sesotho: Ntle le letlole la tshohanyetso, litshenyehelo tse sa lebellwang li baka sekoloto. Boloka likhoeli tse 3-6 tsa litshenyehelo.

lesson.sesotho: Matlole a tshohanyetso a thibela mathata.
